value.title: Code-enforced non-emergency refusal layer
value.description: Close the production-grade guardrail gap: the {kind:'refuse'} verdict already exists in GuardrailVerdict (src/medical/types.ts:14) and the 'refuse' AuditEvent exists (src/medical/types.ts:69), but MedicalGuardrails.evaluate (src/medical/guardrails.ts:80-98) never emits refuse — prescription/dosing/treatment-plan prompts fall through to {kind:'allow'} and are only refused prompt-only by the LLM. Add a deterministic, pure, synchronous RefusalDetector (sibling to RedFlagDetector, src/medical/red-flag.ts) that classifies a prompt into prescription | specific-dosing | individualized-treatment-plan | none. Wire MedicalGuardrails.evaluate to run RedFlagDetector FIRST (short-circuit wins), then RefusalDetector, returning {kind:'refuse', rule, reason} with FIXED never-model-generated reason text (mirror the canned escalation strings at guardrails.ts:30-39). Add a refuse-dispatch branch in MedicalSopEngine.run mirroring the existing consent-refuse path (engine.ts:217-248): return a MedicalAnswer carrying the canned reason with shortCircuit:true, append an audit entry event:'refuse' with ruleId/rulesetVersion/patternsetVersion (IDs/enums only), and reach ZERO downstream numerics/retrieval/LLM. GuardrailContext stays empty (ADR-3). This sprint is self-contained, has no network, and does not touch WHOOP.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and zero typecheck errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
The full test suite passes with zero failures including new collocated src/medical/refusal*.test.ts (npm run test); no regression in the pre-existing suite.

RefusalDetector.detect(prompt) returns category 'prescription' for prescription requests, 'specific-dosing' for specific dose requests, 'individualized-treatment-plan' for personalized treatment/care-plan requests, and 'none' otherwise; it is pure and synchronous (no async/fs/network/LLM) and exposes a patternsetVersion. A unit test covers each category plus benign 'none' cases.

MedicalGuardrails.evaluate returns {kind:'refuse', rule, reason} for each refuse category with FIXED reason text (asserted byte-equal to a constant, proving it is not model-generated), and still returns {kind:'allow'} for benign prompts.

When a prompt matches BOTH a red-flag and a refuse pattern, evaluate returns the red-flag {kind:'short-circuit'} (emergency precedence), not refuse. A unit test constructs such a prompt and asserts short-circuit wins.

MedicalSopEngine.run on a refuse-category prompt returns a MedicalAnswer with body===the canned reason, shortCircuit:true, abstained:false, citations:[], and appends exactly one audit entry with event:'refuse' carrying ruleId/rulesetVersion/patternsetVersion and NO prompt text or health values.

On a refuse-category prompt, an injected spy LLMClient is invoked 0 times and NumericsQueryLayer / FactStore / LiteratureRetriever are never reached (0 LLM, 0 egress) — asserted with a spy that fails if called, mirroring the red-flag spy assertion at engine.ts:53-56.

No network/LLM import is added under src/medical for this sprint and the scoped ESLint medical boundary still passes (npm run lint); RefusalDetector and the guardrails change introduce no @anthropic-ai/sdk, openai, or node:net/http imports.

nonGoals: Do not add WHOOP, any egress axis, or any network code (Sprints 2-3).
Do not add fields to GuardrailContext — it stays the empty placeholder (ADR-3).
Do not use an LLM or in-line model filter for refusal classification — deterministic patterns only (research REFUTED the LLM policy filter).
Do not change RedFlagDetector behavior or the existing short-circuit/consent/allow paths beyond inserting the refuse branch.
Do not alter the MedicalSopEngine.run signature or the zero-arg constructor.
stopConditions: A refuse-category prompt yields a code-enforced refusal + 'refuse' audit entry with 0 LLM calls, red-flag still wins over refuse, benign prompts still allow, and the build/typecheck/test/lint gates are green with no regression

GuardrailContext unchanged. Collocated tests cover detection, fixed-text, red-flag precedence, engine dispatch + audit, and the spy-LLM-never-called assertion. Build, typecheck, test, and lint pass with no regression.

value.title: WHOOP egress axis + authenticated transport
value.description: Establish authenticated, egress-gated access to WHOOP without yet persisting data. Add a third EgressAxis value 'device-connection' to src/medical/egress.ts:5 (default false), widen EgressGuard.isAllowed/assertAllowed to handle all three axes exhaustively (compile-time never check) and EgressGuard.fromConfig to read medical.egress.deviceConnection; add medical.egress.deviceConnection: z.boolean().default(false) to the medical config schema (src/config/schema.ts). The axis-independence invariant MUST hold: enabling any one axis never enables another. Add WhoopTokenStore (src/medical/whoop/whoop-token.ts): clientCredentials() reads WHOOP_CLIENT_ID/WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET from process.env (mirroring src/providers/factory.ts:96-136) and throws clearly if unset; readRefreshToken()/writeTokens() persist {accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAtIso} at .bober/medical/whoop-token.json with mode 0600 (mirror audit.ts 0600). Add WhoopClient (src/medical/whoop/whoop-client.ts) as the SECOND ESLint-excepted network file (sibling to retrieval/medline-source.ts): ensureAccessToken() does the offline-scope refresh_token grant; fetchPage(collection, window, cursor?) fetches one v2 page (recovery=/v2/recovery, sleep=/v2/activity/sleep, cycle=/v2/cycle, workout=/v2/activity/workout), follows the cursor for pagination, refreshes+retries ONCE on 401, and awaits the Reset-header seconds on 429. WhoopClient calls EgressGuard.assertAllowed('device-connection') BEFORE any HTTP. Transport is an injectable FetchLike (mirror medline-source.ts FetchLike) so tests use fixtures, never the real network. Add the new file to the eslint.config.js network-exception allow-list. No sync/persistence/CLI this sprint (Sprint 3).

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and zero typecheck errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck), including the widened EgressAxis exhaustive switch with the compile-time never guard intact.

EgressAxis === 'cloud-inference' | 'literature-retrieval' | 'device-connection'; EgressGuard.fromConfig reads medical.egress.deviceConnection (default false) and the config schema parses a config with deviceConnection true/false/absent. A unit test asserts the TS union and Zod enum/flags agree and that absent => false.

Axis independence: a guard built with only device-connection enabled returns isAllowed('device-connection')===true and isAllowed('cloud-inference')===isAllowed('literature-retrieval')===false; and enabling only one of the original two leaves device-connection false. A unit test asserts all independence combinations.

WhoopClient.ensureAccessToken and fetchPage call EgressGuard.assertAllowed('device-connection') before any HTTP; with the axis off, both throw (Egress axis 'device-connection' not enabled) and the injected FetchLike is never called. A unit test asserts the throw and zero fetch calls.

All WHOOP network access lives only in src/medical/whoop/whoop-client.ts; that file is on the eslint.config.js network-exception allow-list and npm run lint passes; grep confirms no network import (node:http(s)/net/fetch/undici) elsewhere under src/medical including whoop-token.ts and the sync adapter scaffolding.

WhoopTokenStore.clientCredentials() throws a clear 'set WHOOP_CLIENT_ID/WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET' error when either env var is unset; writeTokens() writes .bober/medical/whoop-token.json with file mode 0600; readRefreshToken() returns undefined when the file is absent and the parsed refresh token when present. A unit test (temp dir, env stubbed) asserts each.

With the axis enabled and an injected FetchLike serving fixtures, WhoopClient.fetchPage paginates via cursor across multiple pages, refreshes the access token + retries exactly once on a 401 then succeeds, and on a 429 awaits the Reset-header seconds (injected/fake clock or zero-delay) before retrying — asserted with no real network access.

nonGoals: Do not implement WhoopSyncAdapter, record->HealthObservation mapping, persistence, or the CLI (Sprint 3).
Do not add OS keychain storage — env vars + 0600 sidecar only (ADR-2).
Do not implement webhooks or any inbound listener.
Do not change the existing two egress axes' behavior or the literature-retrieval/cloud-inference call sites.
Do not add a persisted sync cursor (Open Question; idempotent re-run lands in Sprint 3).
stopConditions: The third device-connection axis exists (default false, independent), WhoopTokenStore loads env creds + persists a 0600 token, WhoopClient performs egress-gated paginated v2 fetch with 401-refresh-retry-once and 429-Reset handling against an injected FetchLike, network code is confined to the one ESLint-excepted file, and build/typecheck/test/lint are green

value.title: WHOOP sync adapter + CLI
value.description: The end-to-end visible slice: pull WHOOP data and persist it. Add WhoopSyncAdapter (src/medical/whoop/whoop-sync.ts) with sync(window, sink): Promise<IngestionResult>. It does NOT implement IngestionAdapter (that contract is file-path-shaped, ADR-1) — its entry point is a network sync(window). For each collection in [recovery, sleep, cycle, workout] it loops WhoopClient.fetchPage following the cursor, maps each WhoopRecord to HealthObservation[] (source='whoop', a fixed metric name + fixed unit per collection field; tStart from the record's start ISO; id left to the store's content-derived SHA-256), and writes via the EXISTING ObservationSink.writeBatch in bounded batches (reuse StoreObservationSink + HealthDataStore.upsertObservations unchanged). Resume is idempotent: re-running over an overlapping window inserts only genuinely-new rows via INSERT OR IGNORE; a mid-pagination failure aborts with committed batches intact and never partially corrupts the store (fail-closed, never fail-open). Add the CLI: `bober medical whoop sync [--since <iso>]` in src/cli/commands/medical.ts mirroring the existing `medical import` command (src/cli/commands/medical.ts:30-72): build EgressGuard.fromConfig + WhoopTokenStore + WhoopClient + WhoopSyncAdapter + StoreObservationSink + HealthDataStore, call egress.assertAllowed('device-connection') (surfacing a clear 'not enabled' message), run the sync over the window (default last 7 days or --since), print the IngestionResult {recordsParsed, newRows}, store.close() in finally, set process.exitCode on error and NEVER throw.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and zero typecheck errors (npm run typecheck).

WhoopSyncAdapter.sync(window, sink) pulls all four collections via WhoopClient (injected, fixture-backed), maps records to HealthObservation rows with source='whoop' and a fixed metric+unit per mapped field, writes them through ObservationSink.writeBatch in bounded batches, and returns IngestionResult {recordsParsed, newRows}. A unit test with a fixture WhoopClient and an in-temp-dir HealthDataStore asserts rows land with source='whoop' and the counts are correct.

Idempotent resume: running sync twice over the same/overlapping window yields newRows>0 on the first run and newRows===0 on the second (INSERT OR IGNORE on the content-derived SHA-256 dedup key), with no duplicate observations in the store. A unit test asserts the second run adds zero rows.

Partial-failure safety: when the fixture WhoopClient throws mid-pagination (after >=1 committed batch), sync rejects/aborts, the already-committed batch rows remain valid in the store, no partial/corrupt row is written, and a subsequent successful re-run reaches the same end-state. A unit test asserts committed rows survive and a re-run completes.

`bober medical whoop sync` with the device-connection axis OFF prints a clear 'device-connection egress not enabled' message and exits with process.exitCode 1 without throwing and without constructing a WhoopClient that performs HTTP. A test invoking the command action asserts the message and exit code.

With the axis on but WHOOP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET unset, or with no stored refresh token, the command prints a clear 'set WHOOP_CLIENT_ID/WHOOP_CLIENT_SECRET' or 'authorize first' message and exits with process.exitCode 1 (never throws). A test asserts each branch.

The full test suite passes (npm run test) with no regression and the scoped ESLint medical boundary still passes (npm run lint) — whoop-sync.ts and the CLI contain no network imports (all HTTP remains in whoop-client.ts).

On a successful sync the command prints recordsParsed and newRows and calls HealthDataStore.close() in a finally block (no leaked DB handle); ingestion writes an audit entry event:'ingest' (IDs/enums only) consistent with the existing import path. A test asserts the printed result and the audit entry.

nonGoals: Do not add a persisted sync cursor / checkpoint (Open Question; rely on idempotent re-run, ADR-4).
Do not add UUID-keyed upsert or in-place-mutation handling (Open Question; content-derived dedup only).
Do not add new numerics primitives for WHOOP metrics — reuse the existing closed whitelist.
Do not modify the IngestionAdapter interface, ObservationSink, or the health_observations schema.
Do not add webhooks; sync is on-demand only.
stopConditions: `bober medical whoop sync` persists WHOOP observations end-to-end with deterministic idempotent dedup, fails closed on partial errors, surfaces clear axis-off/credential errors with exit code 1 and never throws, all HTTP stays in whoop-client.ts, and build/typecheck/test/lint are green with no regression

Read FIRST: src/medical/whoop/whoop-client.ts + whoop-token.ts (from Sprint 2 — the sync depends on these), src/medical/ingestion.ts (IngestionNormalizer, ObservationSink, StoreObservationSink, bounded-batch backpressure pattern), src/medical/health-store.ts:32-42,155-175 (content-derived SHA-256 id + upsertObservations INSERT OR IGNORE returning new-row count), src/medical/adapters/apple-health.ts:13,96-99 (bounded ~1000-row batch + writeBatch backpressure precedent), src/cli/commands/medical.ts:30-72 (the `medical import` command shape: action, print, store.close() in finally, process.exitCode on error, never throw), src/medical/types.ts (IngestionResult :191-194, HealthObservation :96-107, AuditEvent 'ingest').

whoop-sync.ts (NO network import — it depends on WhoopClient, which owns HTTP): class WhoopSyncAdapter { readonly source='whoop'; constructor(private client: WhoopClient) {} async sync(window: SyncWindow, sink: ObservationSink): Promise<IngestionResult> }. For each collection in ['recovery','sleep','cycle','workout']: cursor=undefined; do { page = await client.fetchPage(collection, window, cursor); const obs = mapWhoopRecords(collection, page.records); accumulate recordsParsed += obs.length; await sink.writeBatch(obs, []); cursor = page.nextCursor } while (cursor). Sum newRows from the sink/store path. mapWhoopRecords: a small fixed table mapping known WHOOP fields to (metric, unit) with source='whoop', tStart=record.tStartIso, value=number; skip fields not in the table.
